title: A Ember for the Wolf Revisited
premise: Rafael Fairweather, cartographer and ledger-keeper for the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers that the child at his door speaks the First Tongue — the language in which souls are written. The child is a living index of a soul sold generations ago to the court beneath the mountain, and the usurper Veyra marches on the free cities to claim that soul's power for herself. Rafael, whose own memories have been quietly edited by guild oaths, must journey beneath the mountain with the child and a disgraced wolf-knight to steal the soul back before Veyra's armies arrive. In the end Rafael learns he himself was once part of what was sold; he restores the soul to the child, shatters his guild's ledgers, and chooses exile over power as the free cities hold.
about_author: Q. M. Pemberton is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist. They write fantasy about paperwork, memory, and the quiet violence of institutions.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A routine night of balancing the guild's impossible accounts is interrupted when a mud-splattered child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom — and the ledgers begin writing themselves in response. Beat: unease curdling into wonder.

chapters.title: What the Oath Took
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Interrogated by guild masters, Rafael realizes gaps in his own memory align suspiciously with entries about 'the mountain debt.' The child, Wren, recognizes him from something he cannot remember. Beat: dread of one's own past.

chapters.title: A Knight Without a Pack
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera Voss, exiled wolf-knight, is hired by the guild to escort Rafael and Wren east. She distrusts cartographers on principle but sees the usurper's scouts burning villages along the road. Beat: reluctant loyalty kindling.

chapters.title: The Map That Lies
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The trio follows a guild map that deliberately routes them through Veyra's territory — someone inside wants them caught. An ambush costs their supplies and reveals Wren can rewrite small truths by speaking. Beat: betrayal and awe.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sheltering in a drowned free city, Sera tells Rafael why she broke her oath: her pack was ordered to forget a massacre, and she refused. Rafael admits his memories feel borrowed. Beat: two broken people finding kinship.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Descending under the mountain, they find a court of the sold and forgotten, ruled by a broker who keeps souls as collateral. The broker offers Rafael his missing years in exchange for Wren. Beat: temptation at its most intimate.

chapters.title: Veyra Ascendant
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Captured briefly by the usurper's vanguard, Wren glimpses Veyra's mind — she wants the soul not for power but because she sold her own long ago and it lives in fragments. Beat: horror softened by terrible pity.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The broker demands payment: a name freely given. Sera offers hers, dissolving into the court's ledgers, buying Rafael and Wren passage to the vault where the soul is kept. Beat: sacrifice as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: Ember
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. In the vault Rafael recovers his stolen memory: he helped sell the soul as a young guild clerk, and Wren is its heir. He tears the entry from the master ledger, restoring the soul to Wren as Veyra's army breaches the mountain. Beat: climax — guilt transmuted into repair.

chapters.title: Unmapped
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The restored soul's return destabilizes both courts; Veyra retreats to reclaim her scattered self, and the free cities hold. Rafael burns the guild's ledgers, carries Sera's name north, and begins mapping a country that belongs to no one. Beat: bittersweet belonging, chosen rather than granted.
